fields.Name: blackbaud
fields.Description: Blackbaud SKY API connector for Raiser's Edge NXT (nonprofit CRM): Constituent, Gift, Fundraising, Prospect/Opportunity. OAuth2 auth-code + subscription-key header. Other SKY API families out of scope -- see Configuration.OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: SKY API requires TWO credential parts on every request, confirmed from two independent Blackbaud-owned GitHub tutorial repos (blackbaud/sky-api-tutorial-auth-code-nodejs, blackbaud/sky-api-tutorial-auth-code-c-sharp) and the vendor's own docs-source repo (blackbaud/sky-api-docs, includes/basics/{subscription,requestheaders}.md) plus the live developer.blackbaud.com/skyapi/docs/basics page (rendered 2026-06-29): (1) OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow access token in 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', and (2) a static SKY API subscription key in the 'Bb-Api-Subscription-Key' header (vendor docs prose capitalize it 'Bb-Api-Subscription-Key'; vendor SAMPLE CODE sends the literal lowercase key 'bb-api-subscription-key' -- HTTP header names are case-insensitive per RFC 7230 so both forms are valid on the wire; connector code should send it exactly as sampled: 'bb-api-subscription-key'). Both parts are REQUIRED on every call; missing the subscription key or the bearer token independently returns 401. This credential pair is NOT exercised this run -- no credential is available; both parts are documented only.

OAuthEndpoints.note: Confirmed identically across all 4 in-scope OpenAPI specs' securityDefinitions.skyApiOAuth (constituents.swagger.json, gifts.swagger.json, fundraising.swagger.json, prospects.swagger.json) -- flow: accessCode (OAuth2 authorization-code).

Configuration.SubscriptionKeyHeaderNote: The 'Bb-Api-Subscription-Key' (docs prose) / 'bb-api-subscription-key' (sample code, exact literal sent on the wire) header carries the developer account's SKY API subscription key (primary or secondary -- both equally functional). Obtained from the developer's My Subscriptions page after subscribing to a SKY API product tier. This is the SECOND credential part alongside the OAuth2 bearer token -- NOT a substitute for it.
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: Confirmed from the live vendor tutorial (developer.blackbaud.com/skyapi/docs/authorization/auth-code-flow/confidential-application/tutorial, rendered 2026-06-29): access tokens expire after 60 minutes (sample response 'expires_in': 3599). On expiry, calls return 401 with message 'The required Authorization header was missing or invalid, or the token has expired'. Refresh via POST to the token URL with grant_type=refresh_token + the prior refresh_token. Refresh tokens use a SLIDING 365-day expiration window by default -- each refresh issues a NEW refresh_token (refresh_token_expires_in: 31536000) unless the request sets preserve_refresh_token=true, which keeps the same refresh_token and its original expiration. A refresh_token is only ever returned when the exchange used a client_secret (confidential/server-side app flow) -- matches the SKY API being a confidential (client_secret-bearing) OAuth2 app in the prior connector's ClientID/ClientSecret config shape.

universalPK.note: Confirmed from the OpenAPI response schemas across all 4 in-scope families: every Created<X> response definition (e.g. ConstituentApi.CreatedIndividualConstituent, ConstituentApi.CreatedOrganizationConstituent) exposes exactly one property named 'id' as the new record's identifier, and every {resource}/{id} path template names the same 'id'-shaped segment (e.g. /constituent/v1/constituents/{constituent_id}, /gift/v1/gifts/{gift_id}). Blackbaud's per-object ID field is typically named '<object>_id' in path templates but always surfaces as a bare numeric-string 'id' in collection/create responses -- this is a vendor-wide convention, not proven per-object here (per-object IsPrimaryKey verification is the ioiof-extractor's job).

PaginationDefaults.note: Confirmed directly from the OpenAPI spec (constituents.swagger.json: GET /constituent/v1/constituents declares query params limit(integer)/offset(integer); response schema ConstituentApi.ApiCollectionOfConstituentRead = { count, value:[...] }) AND from the vendor's own docs-source repo (blackbaud/sky-api-docs includes/basics/pagination.md) AND the live rendered docs/basics page (2026-06-29): 'When an endpoint supports pagination, it will accept limit and offset query string parameters... limit represents page size, offset represents records to skip.' Some paginated endpoints (per the same source) may ALSO include a next_link hypermedia property in the collection response for fetching the next page, but limit/offset is the base, universally-documented mechanism -- CHECK constraint on IntegrationObject.PaginationType has no 'Cursor+Offset' hybrid value, so this is recorded as Offset (matches the CHECK enum) with next_link noted as a same-family optional accelerator, not a separate pagination type.

Configuration.IncrementalSyncNote: Confirmed from the OpenAPI spec: GET /constituent/v1/constituents declares 'date_added' and 'last_modified' query parameters (both string/date-filter typed) usable as incremental-sync filters. IMPORTANT REQUEST-VS-RESPONSE NAME SPLIT: the request-side incremental filter param is named 'last_modified' (query string), but the corresponding value tracked as the max-watermark comes back on the RESPONSE record under a DIFFERENT field name, 'date_modified' (confirmed present across 10 of the in-scope OpenAPI specs -- church-mgmt, constituents, fundraising, fenxt-gl, fenxt-payable, gifts, prospects, renxt-combined, renxt-reports, renxt-events, renxt-interactions -- as a response-body property distinct from the 'last_modified' query parameter name). This is NOT the same name used twice -- a connector that assumes IncrementalWatermarkField (read from the response to compute max-watermark-seen) is the same literal string as the query parameter it sends on the NEXT request will silently read/write the wrong field. FetchChanges MUST maintain an explicit mapping: send the filter as 'last_modified=<watermark>' on the request, but read/track the new high-watermark from the response field 'date_modified' (per SourceFieldInfo/IncrementalWatermarkField semantics in packages/Integration/engine/src/types.ts:371-374, which name the response-observed field, not the request query-param name). Per-object confirmation of which families expose an equivalent last-modified filter (and confirming the exact response field name per object) is the ioiof-extractor's job; this flag records that the vendor's REST surface supports date-filtered incremental queries at the integration level, not that every in-scope object has one.
Configuration.APIVersioningNote: Confirmed from the OpenAPI specs: each family is versioned via a /{family}/v1/ path segment (e.g. /constituent/v1/, /gift/v1/, /fundraising/v1/, /opportunity/v1/, /nxt-data-integration/v1/). No header-based or accept-header versioning observed in any of the 4 in-scope specs.
Configuration.WebhooksNote: Confirmed live (developer.blackbaud.com/skyapi/products/renxt/webhook, rendered 2026-06-29): a separate RENXT Webhook API exists with event types for Constituent, Gift, Opportunity, and Prospect. Payloads follow the CloudEvents v1.0 spec (Content-Type: application/cloudevents+json), NOT a vendor-specific envelope: { type, specversion, source, subject, id, time, data }. 'data' carries only the changed record's id -- callers must call back into SKY API for full record detail (webhook is a change-notification, not a payload-delivery mechanism). This is a SEPARATE product/spec from the 4 in-scope OpenAPI files this run models deeply (no webhook spec file is in this run's sources/openapi/ corpus) -- recorded here as an integration-level fact, not modeled as a syncable IO this run.
Configuration.WebhooksValidationNote: Confirmed live (developer.blackbaud.com/skyapi/docs/webhooks/subscriptions, rendered 2026-06-29): SKY API webhooks do NOT send a vendor-computed HMAC/signature header. Validation instead follows the CloudEvents 'Abuse Protection' handshake (subscription enters a Provisioning state; the vendor calls the receiving endpoint to validate reachability within a 5-minute window before flipping to Provisioned) plus a caller-chosen shared secret carried as an ordinary query-string parameter on the subscribed URL (vendor's own example: 'https://example.org/bb/handler?webhookKey=<secret>' -- the receiving application defines the param name/value and rejects requests where it doesn't match). There is no vendor-side request-body signature to verify.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: No dedicated bulk/batch-write endpoint family was found in any of the 4 in-scope OpenAPI specs (constituents/gifts/fundraising/prospects) -- e.g. no POST .../batch or .../bulk path. The '/gift-batch/v1' path family (present in gifts.swagger.json) manages RENXT's own Gift Batch UI construct (a batch of gift entries pending commit inside Raiser's Edge NXT itself), which is a domain object, not a connector-level bulk-write API -- left as a candidate IO for the ioiof-extractor, not treated as bulk-operations infrastructure here.
Configuration.ErrorResponseShapeNote: Confirmed from the vendor's own docs-source repo (blackbaud/sky-api-docs includes/basics/{ratelimits,quotas}.md) and the live rendered docs/basics page (2026-06-29), which both show the identical concrete example bodies: 429 rate-limit -> {"statusCode": 429, "message": "Rate limit is exceeded. Try again in 1 second."}; 403 quota-exceeded -> {"statusCode": 403, "message": "Out of call volume quota. Quota will be replenished in 00:06:46."}. Both also carry a 'Retry-After' response header (seconds to wait) in addition to the JSON body. The 4 in-scope OpenAPI specs do not declare formal error response schemas (only descriptions), so this shape is sourced from vendor docs prose/examples, not the spec itself.

RateLimitPolicy.note: CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: an archived vendor docs-source file (github.com/blackbaud/sky-api-docs, includes/basics/ratelimits.md, last content change 2017-08-21) states 'the current rate limit... is 5 calls per second' -- but the LIVE vendor docs page (developer.blackbaud.com/skyapi/docs/basics, rendered via a JS-rendering fetch on 2026-06-29) currently states 'Our rate limit is currently 10 calls per second' and shows a Standard-APIs-subscription-tiers table with Standard = 25,000 calls per 24-hour period (total). The 2017 file is superseded -- Blackbaud has evidently raised the rate limit since 2017. The CURRENT (2026-06-29) live vendor statement is used as the authoritative value: 10 req/s, 25,000 calls/day (Standard tier -- the tier used unless a customer/partner has an upgraded Free/High-volume/Max-volume/Partner tier, which range 1,000 to 250,000 calls/day per the same live table). This also matches the prior BlackbaudConnector.ts implementation comment ('Rate limits: 10 calls/second hard limit') and third-party corroboration (support.ipaas.com integration docs, live-fetched: 'Blackbaud SKY API Free tier allows 10 calls per second and 1,000 calls per 24-hour period').

WriteCapability.note: Confirmed from the OpenAPI specs: Create (POST) and Update (PATCH) operations are broadly present across the in-scope families (e.g. POST /constituent/v1/virtual/individuals creates an individual constituent, response body { id }; PATCH /constituent/v1/constituents/{constituent_id} updates one). DELETE operations are sparse -- only 1 DELETE endpoint found across all 4 in-scope specs combined (DELETE /constituent/v1/constituentcodes/{constituent_code_id}, a constituent SUB-object, not the top-level Constituent/Gift/Fundraiser/Prospect records themselves). Per-object write-capability detail (which specific IOs support which CRUD ops) is the ioiof-extractor's job; this integration-level summary records that the vendor API supports writes at all, gating whether bidirectional sync is even architecturally possible -- it does NOT authorize enabling it (see DefaultSyncDirection).

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No ETag, If-Match, If-Unmodified-Since, or record-version field was found in the 4 in-scope OpenAPI response/request schemas, nor in any vendor docs page reviewed (basics, authorization, pagination, response, webhooks). Blackbaud SKY API updates (PATCH) appear to be last-write-wins with no optimistic-concurrency primitive exposed to API consumers. Absent evidence of a concurrency token, conflict handling can only be snapshot/3-way, never a real MostRecent resolution keyed on a vendor-supplied version marker.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsDetail: The single DELETE endpoint found (constituent codes sub-object) gives no evidence either way on hard-vs-soft delete for the records this run models. No 'is_deleted'/'inactive'/archive-flag field was documented on the top-level Constituent/Gift/Fundraiser/Prospect resources in the reviewed OpenAPI schemas or docs pages. The RENXT Webhook API DOES define a delete event type (e.g. com.blackbaud.constituent.delete.v1, confirmed live from developer.blackbaud.com/skyapi/docs/webhooks/overview's own worked example), which at minimum proves deletes ARE a first-class, notifiable event in the underlying RENXT system -- but that does not by itself establish whether the SKY API's own delete semantics (for objects that do expose a DELETE verb) are hard or soft. Left unconfirmed rather than guessed; per-object delete-behavior verification (including any 'inactive'-flag pattern) is the ioiof-extractor's job when it examines specific object schemas.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Per project convention, EVERY object defaults to Pull (read-only) regardless of the vendor's write capability. Bidirectional sync against a client's live Raiser's Edge NXT data is opt-in only, and only after a sandbox validation -- see the preconditions below.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReason: No ConcurrencyControl primitive (no ETag/If-Match/version field) is exposed by SKY API, so MostRecent cannot be implemented with any integrity -- there is no vendor-supplied timestamp/version to arbitrate a genuine conflict. SourceWins (Blackbaud RENXT wins) is the safer default IF bidirectional is ever enabled, because RENXT is virtually always the fundraising organization's system of record for constituent/gift data; DestWins would silently overwrite a nonprofit's canonical donor/gift records from a secondary system. This is a RECOMMENDATION for a future bidirectional EntityMap only -- DefaultSyncDirection stays Pull by default regardless.
Configuration.BidirectionalPreconditions: Before ANY EntityMap for this connector is switched off Pull, ALL of the following must be true and validated against a sandbox/test RENXT environment first: (1) Delete semantics for the specific target object must be independently confirmed hard vs soft (not established this run -- see DeleteSemanticsDetail) so orphan-deletion / tombstone propagation is provably safe; (2) Because ConcurrencyControl is 'none', conflict resolution can only be snapshot/3-way or a fixed policy (SourceWins recommended) -- MostRecent must NOT be offered as a resolution option for this connector until/unless a vendor-side version marker is discovered; (3) The per-object CRUD surface (which of Create/Update/Delete each specific target IO actually supports) must be confirmed via the ioiof-extractor's per-operation extraction, since this run found DELETE support to be sparse/inconsistent across objects; (4) A live round-trip write test (create/update/delete a disposable test record) must succeed against a sandbox or test-tier SKY API subscription before any write path is exercised against a client's production RENXT environment, per the 'Read-only, ceiling T8' testing discipline -- this run has NO credential and therefore proves none of this empirically; it is documented, not exercised.
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: No vendor-documented custom-field naming/marker convention (comparable to HubSpot's custom-property naming or a 'p_<accountID>_<name>' style prefix) was found in the reviewed OpenAPI specs or docs pages. RENXT DOES support user-defined 'custom fields' as a first-class concept (e.g. POST /constituent/v1/constituents/customfields in the OpenAPI spec, and a dedicated 'Custom Field' product-doc section confirmed in the live site nav), but they are modeled as a distinct queryable sub-resource (an attached custom-field record with its own id/category/value), not as a marked/prefixed field name on the parent object's own schema. Left null rather than guessing a prefix pattern that does not exist.
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNote: No vendor-documented convention for marking a customer-created custom OBJECT (as opposed to a custom field on a standard object) was found. RENXT's customization model, per the reviewed docs, is custom-FIELDS-on-standard-objects rather than fully custom object types (unlike e.g. Salesforce or HubSpot custom objects).

Real RENXT companion services, NOT requested in the 20-leaf taxonomy list. Kept in-tree as reachable Tier-1 sources for a future taxonomy-expansion request -- not modeled today because they weren't asked for, not because they're low-quality.

Configuration.OutOfScopeScopeReason: operator-scoped subset is the client-relevant/reachable surface for a nonprofit-CRM use case

AdditionalObservations.Value: Vendor docs PROSE renders the header name as 'Bb-Api-Subscription-Key' (title-case); vendor SAMPLE CODE (2 independent GitHub tutorial repos) sends the literal lowercase 'bb-api-subscription-key'. HTTP header field names are case-insensitive (RFC 7230 3.2), so both are functionally identical on the wire -- but connector code should match the SAMPLE-CODE casing exactly since that is what a working, vendor-published client actually transmits.

A 2017-vintage vendor docs-source snapshot states 5 calls/second; the current (2026-06-29) live vendor page states 10 calls/second. Treated as a documented rate increase over time, not an unresolved contradiction -- current live source wins. See RateLimitPolicy.note for the full resolution chain.
